answer:
Based on the available source-attributed candidate evidence (not independently clinically verified):
- MedlinePlus names brain injury among possible causes of epilepsy, while noting that the cause is often unknown. [Evidence: PHASE2_CAND_0015; https://medlineplus.gov/epilepsy.html]
- The Epilepsy Foundation explains that TBI can cause cerebral contusions, hemorrhage, edema, diffuse axonal injury and brain scarring. These establish structural brain injury after trauma. The article also associates certain brain injuries with later seizures and epilepsy but does not explicitly establish the complete process of epileptogenic neural circuit remodeling. [Evidence: PHASE2_CAND_0054; https://www.epilepsy.com/causes/structural/traumatic-brain-injury-epilepsy]
- NINDS identifies traumatic brain injury and brain damage as possible causes of epilepsy. It explains that attempts by the brain to repair itself following head injury may create abnormal nerve connections capable of producing seizures. The source also discusses increased recurrence risk following seizures in people with prior structural brain problems. [Evidence: PHASE2_CAND_0057; https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/epilepsy-and-seizures]
- The review explains that traumatic injury-associated neuronal loss, gliosis, neuroinflammation and abnormal neural circuit reorganization can promote epileptogenesis. Altered excitation-inhibition balance and recurrent excitatory connections can increase susceptibility to spontaneous recurrent seizures. Post-traumatic epilepsy is distinguished from acute provoked seizures by delayed unprovoked seizure occurrence and high recurrence risk. [Evidence: PHASE2_CAND_0056; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12257072/]
